newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: BANCO ESPIRITO AIMS GLOBAL IN SAFRICA DEAL.
newsitem.headline: BANCO ESPIRITO AIMS GLOBAL IN SAFRICA DEAL.

text.p: A new joint venture with South African life assurer Old Mutual is part of Portugal's Grupo Banco Espirito Santo's drive to become more international, executive vice president Ricardo Espirito Santo Silva said on Friday.
Speaking in Johannesburg at the announcment of the financial services joint venture, Espirito Santo said:
"Internationalisation is one of the key functions of the bank. This alliance is anoher step in our internationalisation."
The group has over 400 branches in Portugal and is present in 17 countries.
He added that Banco Espirito would soon set up a branch in Luanda, capital of former Portuguese colony Angola.
"We are looking and we already have authorisation to open a full branch in Luanda," he said.

The new company set up with Old Mutual, Novos Navegadores, would be Guernsey-based and will initially focus on the emigrated Portuguese market in South Africa, providing them with investment services and fund management expertise.
The total combined value of assets between Old Mutual and Banco Espirito is $67 billion of which $45 billion was attributed to Old Mutual.
Old Mutual International managing director Frits Vleggaar told reporters that Novos Navegadores could attract investment of up to $10 million in its first year.
"Based on the historical experience that we have around the world we would expect to raise between five and 10 million (dollars) in the first 12 months," he said.

Novos Navegadores has been set up jointly by Old Mutual subsidiary Old Mutual International Financial Services and Espirito Santo Activos Financeiros (ESAF), the asset management unit of the Portugese bank.
Novos Navegadores would be looking for further expansion opportunities, the two companies said in a separate statement.
"As regards further expansion and co-operation in other parts of the world, we undoubtedly will in due course consider such opportunities...," the two companies said.

Based in the Channel Island tax haven of Guernsey, Novos Navegadores will not operate directly from South Africa. Old Mutual representatives will, however, be able to sell some of the new company's products.

Investors' funds will be managed by Old Mutual International Asset Managers, which already oversees assets of over $2.5 billion, in a practical working relationship with ESAF, which manages funds of $4.5 billion.
